## Export a public HTTP server runnable for custom server use

We need to expose the existing internal HTTP server runnable as a public API so users can run their own HTTP servers within a manager without reimplementing the Runnable interface. The exported version should support optional leader election gating, configurable shutdown timeouts, and flexible listener or address configuration. This will let projects like operator-framework run custom servers alongside the manager's built-in ones.

313: // Start starts the manager and waits indefinitely.
314: // There is only two ways to have start return:
315: // An error has occurred during in one of the internal operations,
316: // such as leader election, cache start, webhooks, and so on.
317: // Or, the context is cancelled.
318: func (cm *controllerManager) Start(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
319: 	cm.Lock()
320: 	if cm.started {
321: 		cm.Unlock()
322: 		return errors.New("manager already started")
323: 	}
324: 	cm.started = true
325: 
326: 	var ready bool
327: 	defer func() {
328: 		// Only unlock the manager if we haven't reached
329: 		// the internal readiness condition.
330: 		if !ready {
331: 			cm.Unlock()
332: 		}
333: 	}()
334: 
335: 	// Initialize the internal context.
336: 	cm.internalCtx, cm.internalCancel = context.WithCancel(ctx)
337: 
338: 	// This chan indicates that stop is complete, in other words all runnables have returned or timeout on stop request
339: 	stopComplete := make(chan struct{})
340: 	defer close(stopComplete)
341: 	// This must be deferred after closing stopComplete, otherwise we deadlock.
342: 	defer func() {
343: 		// https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/images/gettyimages-459889618-1533579787.jpg
344: 		stopErr := cm.engageStopProcedure(stopComplete)
345: 		if stopErr != nil {
346: 			if err != nil {
347: 				// Utilerrors.Aggregate allows to use errors.Is for all contained errors
348: 				// whereas fmt.Errorf allows wrapping at most one error which means the
349: 				// other one can not be found anymore.
350: 				err = kerrors.NewAggregate([]error{err, stopErr})
351: 			} else {
352: 				err = stopErr
353: 			}
354: 		}
355: 	}()
356: 
357: 	// Add the cluster runnable.
358: 	if err := cm.add(cm.cluster); err != nil {
359: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to add cluster to runnables: %w", err)
360: 	}
361: 
362: 	// Metrics should be served whether the controller is leader or not.
363: 	// (If we don't serve metrics for non-leaders, prometheus will still scrape
364: 	// the pod but will get a connection refused).
365: 	if cm.metricsServer != nil {
366: 		// Note: We are adding the metrics server directly to HTTPServers here as matching on the
367: 		// metricsserver.Server interface in cm.runnables.Add would be very brittle.
368: 		if err := cm.runnables.HTTPServers.Add(cm.metricsServer, nil); err != nil {
369: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to add metrics server: %w", err)
370: 		}
371: 	}
372: 
373: 	// Serve health probes.
374: 	if cm.healthProbeListener != nil {
375: 		if err := cm.addHealthProbeServer(); err != nil {
376: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to add health probe server: %w", err)
377: 		}
378: 	}
379: 
380: 	// Add pprof server
381: 	if cm.pprofListener != nil {
382: 		if err := cm.addPprofServer(); err != nil {
383: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to add pprof server: %w", err)
384: 		}
385: 	}
386: 
387: 	// First start any internal HTTP servers, which includes health probes, metrics and profiling if enabled.
388: 	//
389: 	// WARNING: Internal HTTP servers MUST start before any cache is populated, otherwise it would block
390: 	// conversion webhooks to be ready for serving which make the cache never get ready.
391: 	if err := cm.runnables.HTTPServers.Start(cm.internalCtx); err != nil {
392: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to start HTTP servers: %w", err)
393: 	}
394: 
395: 	// Start any webhook servers, which includes conversion, validation, and defaulting
396: 	// webhooks that are registered.
397: 	//
398: 	// WARNING: Webhooks MUST start before any cache is populated, otherwise there is a race condition
399: 	// between conversion webhooks and the cache sync (usually initial list) which causes the webhooks
400: 	// to never start because no cache can be populated.
401: 	if err := cm.runnables.Webhooks.Start(cm.internalCtx); err != nil {
402: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to start webhooks: %w", err)
403: 	}
404: 
405: 	// Start and wait for caches.
406: 	if err := cm.runnables.Caches.Start(cm.internalCtx); err != nil {
407: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to start caches: %w", err)
408: 	}
409: 
410: 	// Start the non-leaderelection Runnables after the cache has synced.
411: 	if err := cm.runnables.Others.Start(cm.internalCtx); err != nil {
412: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to start other runnables: %w", err)
413: 	}
414: 
415: 	// Start the leader election and all required runnables.
416: 	{
417: 		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
418: 		cm.leaderElectionCancel = cancel
419: 		go func() {
420: 			if cm.resourceLock != nil {
421: 				if err := cm.startLeaderElection(ctx); err != nil {
422: 					cm.errChan <- err
423: 				}
424: 			} else {
425: 				// Treat not having leader election enabled the same as being elected.
426: 				if err := cm.startLeaderElectionRunnables(); err != nil {
427: 					cm.errChan <- err
428: 				}
429: 				close(cm.elected)
430: 			}
431: 		}()
432: 	}
433: 
434: 	ready = true
435: 	cm.Unlock()
436: 	select {
437: 	case <-ctx.Done():
438: 		// We are done
439: 		return nil
440: 	case err := <-cm.errChan:
441: 		// Error starting or running a runnable
442: 		return err
443: 	}
444: }
445: 
446: // engageStopProcedure signals all runnables to stop, reads potential errors
447: // from the errChan and waits for them to end. It must not be called more than once.
448: func (cm *controllerManager) engageStopProcedure(stopComplete <-chan struct{}) error {
449: 	if !atomic.CompareAndSwapInt64(cm.stopProcedureEngaged, 0, 1) {
450: 		return errors.New("stop procedure already engaged")
451: 	}
452: 
453: 	// Populate the shutdown context, this operation MUST be done before
454: 	// closing the internalProceduresStop channel.
455: 	//
456: 	// The shutdown context immediately expires if the gracefulShutdownTimeout is not set.
457: 	var shutdownCancel context.CancelFunc
458: 	if cm.gracefulShutdownTimeout < 0 {
459: 		// We want to wait forever for the runnables to stop.
460: 		cm.shutdownCtx, shutdownCancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
461: 	} else {
462: 		cm.shutdownCtx, shutdownCancel = context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), cm.gracefulShutdownTimeout)
463: 	}
464: 	defer shutdownCancel()
465: 
466: 	// Start draining the errors before acquiring the lock to make sure we don't deadlock
467: 	// if something that has the lock is blocked on trying to write into the unbuffered
468: 	// channel after something else already wrote into it.
469: 	var closeOnce sync.Once
470: 	go func() {
471: 		for {
472: 			// Closing in the for loop is required to avoid race conditions between
473: 			// the closure of all internal procedures and making sure to have a reader off the error channel.
474: 			closeOnce.Do(func() {
475: 				// Cancel the internal stop channel and wait for the procedures to stop and complete.
476: 				close(cm.internalProceduresStop)
477: 				cm.internalCancel()
478: 			})
479: 			select {
480: 			case err, ok := <-cm.errChan:
481: 				if ok {
482: 					cm.logger.Error(err, "error received after stop sequence was engaged")
483: 				}
484: 			case <-stopComplete:
485: 				return
486: 			}
487: 		}
488: 	}()
489: 
490: 	// We want to close this after the other runnables stop, because we don't
491: 	// want things like leader election to try and emit events on a closed
492: 	// channel
493: 	defer cm.recorderProvider.Stop(cm.shutdownCtx)
494: 	defer func() {
495: 		// Cancel leader election only after we waited. It will os.Exit() the app for safety.
496: 		if cm.resourceLock != nil {
497: 			// After asking the context to be cancelled, make sure
498: 			// we wait for the leader stopped channel to be closed, otherwise
499: 			// we might encounter race conditions between this code
500: 			// and the event recorder, which is used within leader election code.
501: 			cm.leaderElectionCancel()
502: 			<-cm.leaderElectionStopped
503: 		}
504: 	}()
505: 
506: 	go func() {
507: 		// First stop the non-leader election runnables.
508: 		cm.logger.Info("Stopping and waiting for non leader election runnables")
509: 		cm.runnables.Others.StopAndWait(cm.shutdownCtx)
510: 
511: 		// Stop all the leader election runnables, which includes reconcilers.
512: 		cm.logger.Info("Stopping and waiting for leader election runnables")
513: 		// Prevent leader election when shutting down a non-elected manager
514: 		cm.runnables.LeaderElection.startOnce.Do(func() {})
515: 		cm.runnables.LeaderElection.StopAndWait(cm.shutdownCtx)
516: 
517: 		// Stop the caches before the leader election runnables, this is an important
518: 		// step to make sure that we don't race with the reconcilers by receiving more events
519: 		// from the API servers and enqueueing them.
520: 		cm.logger.Info("Stopping and waiting for caches")
521: 		cm.runnables.Caches.StopAndWait(cm.shutdownCtx)
522: 
523: 		// Webhooks and internal HTTP servers should come last, as they might be still serving some requests.
524: 		cm.logger.Info("Stopping and waiting for webhooks")
525: 		cm.runnables.Webhooks.StopAndWait(cm.shutdownCtx)
526: 
527: 		cm.logger.Info("Stopping and waiting for HTTP servers")
528: 		cm.runnables.HTTPServers.StopAndWait(cm.shutdownCtx)
529: 
530: 		// Proceed to close the manager and overall shutdown context.
531: 		cm.logger.Info("Wait completed, proceeding to shutdown the manager")
532: 		shutdownCancel()
533: 	}()
534: 
535: 	<-cm.shutdownCtx.Done()
536: 	if err := cm.shutdownCtx.Err(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
537: 		if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
538: 			if cm.gracefulShutdownTimeout > 0 {
539: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed waiting for all runnables to end within grace period of %s: %w", cm.gracefulShutdownTimeout, err)
540: 			}
541: 			return nil
542: 		}
543: 		// For any other error, return the error.
544: 		return err
545: 	}
546: 
547: 	return nil
548: }
549: 
550: func (cm *controllerManager) startLeaderElectionRunnables() error {
551: 	return cm.runnables.LeaderElection.Start(cm.internalCtx)
552: }
553: 
554: func (cm *controllerManager) startLeaderElection(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
555: 	l, err := leaderelection.NewLeaderElector(leaderelection.LeaderElectionConfig{
556: 		Lock:          cm.resourceLock,
557: 		LeaseDuration: cm.leaseDuration,
558: 		RenewDeadline: cm.renewDeadline,
559: 		RetryPeriod:   cm.retryPeriod,
560: 		Callbacks: leaderelection.LeaderCallbacks{
561: 			OnStartedLeading: func(_ context.Context) {
562: 				if err := cm.startLeaderElectionRunnables(); err != nil {
563: 					cm.errChan <- err
564: 					return
565: 				}
566: 				close(cm.elected)
567: 			},
568: 			OnStoppedLeading: func() {
569: 				if cm.onStoppedLeading != nil {
570: 					cm.onStoppedLeading()
571: 				}
572: 				// Make sure graceful shutdown is skipped if we lost the leader lock without
573: 				// intending to.
574: 				cm.gracefulShutdownTimeout = time.Duration(0)
575: 				// Most implementations of leader election log.Fatal() here.
576: 				// Since Start is wrapped in log.Fatal when called, we can just return
577: 				// an error here which will cause the program to exit.
578: 				cm.errChan <- errors.New("leader election lost")
579: 			},
580: 		},
581: 		ReleaseOnCancel: cm.leaderElectionReleaseOnCancel,
582: 		Name:            cm.leaderElectionID,
583: 	})
584: 	if err != nil {
585: 		return err
586: 	}
587: 
588: 	// Start the leader elector process
589: 	go func() {
590: 		l.Run(ctx)
591: 		<-ctx.Done()
592: 		close(cm.leaderElectionStopped)
593: 	}()
594: 	return nil
595: }

598: 	return cm.elected

47: // Server is a server that serves metrics.
48: type Server interface {
49: 	// NeedLeaderElection implements the LeaderElectionRunnable interface, which indicates
50: 	// the metrics server doesn't need leader election.
51: 	NeedLeaderElection() bool
52: 
53: 	// Start runs the server.
54: 	// It will install the metrics related resources depending on the server configuration.
55: 	Start(ctx context.Context) error
56: }

58: // Options are all available options for the metrics.Server
59: type Options struct {
60: 	// SecureServing enables serving metrics via https.
61: 	// Per default metrics will be served via http.
62: 	SecureServing bool
63: 
64: 	// BindAddress is the bind address for the metrics server.
65: 	// It will be defaulted to ":8080" if unspecified.
66: 	// Set this to "0" to disable the metrics server.
67: 	BindAddress string
68: 
69: 	// ExtraHandlers contains a map of handlers (by path) which will be added to the metrics server.
70: 	// This might be useful to register diagnostic endpoints e.g. pprof.
71: 	// Note that pprof endpoints are meant to be sensitive and shouldn't be exposed publicly.
72: 	// If the simple path -> handler mapping offered here is not enough, a new http
73: 	// server/listener should be added as Runnable to the manager via the Add method.
74: 	ExtraHandlers map[string]http.Handler
75: 
76: 	// FilterProvider provides a filter which is a func that is added around
77: 	// the metrics and the extra handlers on the metrics server.
78: 	// This can be e.g. used to enforce authentication and authorization on the handlers
79: 	// endpoint by setting this field to filters.WithAuthenticationAndAuthorization.
80: 	FilterProvider func(c *rest.Config, httpClient *http.Client) (Filter, error)
81: 
82: 	// CertDir is the directory that contains the server key and certificate. Defaults to
83: 	// <temp-dir>/k8s-metrics-server/serving-certs.
84: 	//
85: 	// Note: This option is only used when TLSOpts does not set GetCertificate.
86: 	// Note: If certificate or key doesn't exist a self-signed certificate will be used.
87: 	CertDir string
88: 
89: 	// CertName is the server certificate name. Defaults to tls.crt.
90: 	//
91: 	// Note: This option is only used when TLSOpts does not set GetCertificate.
92: 	// Note: If certificate or key doesn't exist a self-signed certificate will be used.
93: 	CertName string
94: 
95: 	// KeyName is the server key name. Defaults to tls.key.
96: 	//
97: 	// Note: This option is only used when TLSOpts does not set GetCertificate.
98: 	// Note: If certificate or key doesn't exist a self-signed certificate will be used.
99: 	KeyName string
100: 
101: 	// TLSOpts is used to allow configuring the TLS config used for the server.
102: 	// This also allows providing a certificate via GetCertificate.
103: 	TLSOpts []func(*tls.Config)

105: 	// ListenConfig contains options for listening to an address on the metric server.

109: // Filter is a func that is added around metrics and extra handlers on the metrics server.
110: type Filter func(log logr.Logger, handler http.Handler) (http.Handler, error)

112: // NewServer constructs a new metrics.Server from the provided options.
113: func NewServer(o Options, config *rest.Config, httpClient *http.Client) (Server, error) {
114: 	o.setDefaults()
115: 
116: 	// Skip server creation if metrics are disabled.
117: 	if o.BindAddress == "0" {
118: 		return nil, nil
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	// Validate that ExtraHandlers is not overwriting the default /metrics endpoint.
122: 	if o.ExtraHandlers != nil {
123: 		if _, ok := o.ExtraHandlers[defaultMetricsEndpoint]; ok {
124: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("overriding builtin %s endpoint is not allowed", defaultMetricsEndpoint)
125: 		}
126: 	}
127: 
128: 	// Create the metrics filter if a FilterProvider is set.
129: 	var metricsFilter Filter
130: 	if o.FilterProvider != nil {
131: 		var err error
132: 		metricsFilter, err = o.FilterProvider(config, httpClient)
133: 		if err != nil {
134: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("filter provider failed to create filter for the metrics server: %w", err)
135: 		}
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	return &defaultServer{
139: 		metricsFilter: metricsFilter,
140: 		options:       o,
141: 	}, nil
142: }

144: // defaultServer is the default implementation used for Server.
145: type defaultServer struct {
146: 	options Options

conversation.content:
The dynamic RESTMapper currently returns a plain error (`failed to find API group %q`) when an API group is not present in the cluster. Clients of controller-runtime expect `meta.NoMatchError` (or `meta.NoResourceMatchError` / `meta.NoKindMatchError`) in this case, consistent with what a static RESTMapper returns. This inconsistency breaks callers that use `meta.IsNoMatchError` to decide whether to retry or surface the error.

    The goal is to make the lazy RESTMapper behave like a standard discovery-based RESTMapper for unknown groups:
    - When a requested group (and optional version) does not exist, the RESTMapper methods (`RESTMapping`, `RESTMappings`, `KindFor`, `KindsFor`, `ResourceFor`, `ResourcesFor`) should return a `*meta.NoKindMatchError` or `*meta.NoResourceMatchError` rather than failing with a generic error.
    - When a specific version of an existing group is requested but that version does not exist (404 from the discovery endpoint), that should also not be treated as a hard failure — it should be handled gracefully so the mapper can still return a proper `NoMatchError`.

    Additionally, the existing tests in `pkg/client/apiutil/restmapper_test.go` should be tightened to explicitly assert that the returned errors satisfy `meta.IsNoMatchError` (not just that an error occurred). This will lock in the desired behavior and catch regressions.

    See also PR #2425 which attempted a similar fix; this task should incorporate the same intent.

## Environment Setup
- Check `go.mod` for the Go module setup and dependency versions.
    - Check the `Makefile` for project-specific targets (e.g., test, verify, lint).
    - There is also `hack/verify.sh`, `hack/test-all.sh`, and `hack/check-everything.sh` under `hack/` that may be relevant for full verification.

## Implementation Plan
1. Update `findAPIGroupByName` in `pkg/client/apiutil/restmapper.go` so that when a group is not found in the cache or the server, it returns a `nil` group instead of a `fmt.Errorf("failed to find API group %q")` error. The caller in `addKnownGroupAndReload` should handle the `nil` group gracefully (e.g., skip appending versions).
    2. In `fetchGroupVersionResources`, change the error handling so that a `404 Not Found` from `ServerResourcesForGroupVersion` is not added to `failedGroups` — use `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` to detect this case and skip it.
    3. Verify that all public RESTMapper methods already retry with `addKnownGroupAndReload` on a `NoMatchError`; with the above changes, the underlying `restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper` will be able to produce the correct `NoMatchError` for the missing group/version.

153: // addKnownGroupAndReload reloads the mapper with updated information about missing API group.
154: // versions can be specified for partial updates, for instance for v1beta1 version only.
155: func (m *mapper) addKnownGroupAndReload(groupName string, versions ...string) error {
156: 	// versions will here be [""] if the forwarded Version value of
157: 	// GroupVersionResource (in calling method) was not specified.
158: 	if len(versions) == 1 && versions[0] == "" {
159: 		versions = nil
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	// If no specific versions are set by user, we will scan all available ones for the API group.
163: 	// This operation requires 2 requests: /api and /apis, but only once. For all subsequent calls
164: 	// this data will be taken from cache.
165: 	if len(versions) == 0 {
166: 		apiGroup, err := m.findAPIGroupByName(groupName)
167: 		if err != nil {
168: 			return err
169: 		}
170: 		if apiGroup != nil {
171: 			for _, version := range apiGroup.Versions {
172: 				versions = append(versions, version.Version)
173: 			}
174: 		}
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	m.mu.Lock()
178: 	defer m.mu.Unlock()
179: 
180: 	// Create or fetch group resources from cache.
181: 	groupResources := &restmapper.APIGroupResources{
182: 		Group:              metav1.APIGroup{Name: groupName},
183: 		VersionedResources: make(map[string][]metav1.APIResource),
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	// Update information for group resources about versioned resources.
187: 	// The number of API calls is equal to the number of versions: /apis/<group>/<version>.
188: 	// If we encounter a missing API version (NotFound error), we will remove the group from
189: 	// the m.apiGroups and m.knownGroups caches.
190: 	// If this happens, in the next call the group will be added back to apiGroups
191: 	// and only the existing versions will be loaded in knownGroups.
192: 	groupVersionResources, err := m.fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked(groupName, versions...)
193: 	if err != nil {
194: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get API group resources: %w", err)
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	if _, ok := m.knownGroups[groupName]; ok {
198: 		groupResources = m.knownGroups[groupName]
199: 	}
200: 
201: 	// Update information for group resources about the API group by adding new versions.
202: 	// Ignore the versions that are already registered.
203: 	for groupVersion, resources := range groupVersionResources {
204: 		version := groupVersion.Version
205: 
206: 		groupResources.VersionedResources[version] = resources.APIResources
207: 		found := false
208: 		for _, v := range groupResources.Group.Versions {
209: 			if v.Version == version {
210: 				found = true
211: 				break
212: 			}
213: 		}
214: 
215: 		if !found {
216: 			groupResources.Group.Versions = append(groupResources.Group.Versions, metav1.GroupVersionForDiscovery{
217: 				GroupVersion: metav1.GroupVersion{Group: groupName, Version: version}.String(),
218: 				Version:      version,
219: 			})
220: 		}
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	// Update data in the cache.
224: 	m.knownGroups[groupName] = groupResources
225: 
226: 	// Finally, update the group with received information and regenerate the mapper.
227: 	updatedGroupResources := make([]*restmapper.APIGroupResources, 0, len(m.knownGroups))
228: 	for _, agr := range m.knownGroups {
229: 		updatedGroupResources = append(updatedGroupResources, agr)
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	m.mapper = restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper(updatedGroupResources)
233: 	return nil
234: }
235: 
236: // findAPIGroupByNameLocked returns API group by its name.
237: func (m *mapper) findAPIGroupByName(groupName string) (*metav1.APIGroup, error) {
238: 	// Looking in the cache first.
239: 	{
240: 		m.mu.RLock()
241: 		group, ok := m.apiGroups[groupName]
242: 		m.mu.RUnlock()
243: 		if ok {
244: 			return group, nil
245: 		}
246: 	}
247: 
248: 	// Update the cache if nothing was found.
249: 	apiGroups, err := m.client.ServerGroups()
250: 	if err != nil {
251: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get server groups: %w", err)
252: 	}
253: 	if len(apiGroups.Groups) == 0 {
254: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("received an empty API groups list")
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	m.mu.Lock()
258: 	for i := range apiGroups.Groups {
259: 		group := &apiGroups.Groups[i]
260: 		m.apiGroups[group.Name] = group
261: 	}
262: 	m.mu.Unlock()
263: 
264: 	// Looking in the cache again.
265: 	m.mu.RLock()
266: 	defer m.mu.RUnlock()
267: 
268: 	// Don't return an error here if the API group is not present.
269: 	// The reloaded RESTMapper will take care of returning a NoMatchError.
270: 	return m.apiGroups[groupName], nil
271: }
272: 
273: // fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked fetches the resources for the specified group and its versions.
274: // This method might modify the cache so it needs to be called under the lock.
275: func (m *mapper) fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked(groupName string, versions ...string) (map[schema.GroupVersion]*metav1.APIResourceList, error) {
276: 	groupVersionResources := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]*metav1.APIResourceList)
277: 	failedGroups := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]error)
278: 
279: 	for _, version := range versions {
280: 		groupVersion := schema.GroupVersion{Group: groupName, Version: version}
281: 
282: 		apiResourceList, err := m.client.ServerResourcesForGroupVersion(groupVersion.String())
283: 		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) {
284: 			// If the version is not found, we remove the group from the cache
285: 			// so it gets refreshed on the next call.
286: 			if m.isAPIGroupCached(groupVersion) {
287: 				delete(m.apiGroups, groupName)
288: 			}
289: 			if m.isGroupVersionCached(groupVersion) {
290: 				delete(m.knownGroups, groupName)
291: 			}
292: 			continue
293: 		} else if err != nil {
294: 			failedGroups[groupVersion] = err
295: 		}
296: 
297: 		if apiResourceList != nil {
298: 			// even in case of error, some fallback might have been returned.
299: 			groupVersionResources[groupVersion] = apiResourceList
300: 		}
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	if len(failedGroups) > 0 {
304: 		err := ErrResourceDiscoveryFailed(failedGroups)
305: 		return nil, &err
306: 	}
307: 
308: 	return groupVersionResources, nil
309: }
310: 
311: // isGroupVersionCached checks if a version for a group is cached in the known groups cache.
312: func (m *mapper) isGroupVersionCached(gv schema.GroupVersion) bool {
313: 	if cachedGroup, ok := m.knownGroups[gv.Group]; ok {
314: 		_, cached := cachedGroup.VersionedResources[gv.Version]
315: 		return cached
316: 	}
317: 
318: 	return false
319: }
320: 
321: // isAPIGroupCached checks if a version for a group is cached in the api groups cache.
322: func (m *mapper) isAPIGroupCached(gv schema.GroupVersion) bool {
323: 	cachedGroup, ok := m.apiGroups[gv.Group]
324: 	if !ok {
325: 		return false
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	for _, version := range cachedGroup.Versions {
329: 		if version.Version == gv.Version {
330: 			return true
331: 		}
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	return false
335: }

372: func (t versionedTracker) update(gvr schema.GroupVersionResource, obj runtime.Object, ns string, isStatus bool, deleting bool) error {
373: 	accessor, err := meta.Accessor(obj)
374: 	if err != nil {
375: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get accessor for object: %w", err)
376: 	}
377: 
378: 	if accessor.GetName() == "" {
379: 		return apierrors.NewInvalid(
380: 			obj.GetObjectKind().GroupVersionKind().GroupKind(),
381: 			accessor.GetName(),
382: 			field.ErrorList{field.Required(field.NewPath("metadata.name"), "name is required")})
383: 	}
384: 
385: 	gvk, err := apiutil.GVKForObject(obj, t.scheme)
386: 	if err != nil {
387: 		return err
388: 	}
389: 
390: 	oldObject, err := t.ObjectTracker.Get(gvr, ns, accessor.GetName())
391: 	if err != nil {
392: 		// If the resource is not found and the resource allows create on update, issue a
393: 		// create instead.
394: 		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) && allowsCreateOnUpdate(gvk) {
395: 			return t.Create(gvr, obj, ns)
396: 		}
397: 		return err
398: 	}
399: 
400: 	if t.withStatusSubresource.Has(gvk) {
401: 		if isStatus { // copy everything but status and metadata.ResourceVersion from original object
402: 			if err := copyStatusFrom(obj, oldObject); err != nil {
403: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to copy non-status field for object with status subresouce: %w", err)
404: 			}
405: 			passedRV := accessor.GetResourceVersion()
406: 			if err := copyFrom(oldObject, obj); err != nil {
407: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to restore non-status fields: %w", err)
408: 			}
409: 			accessor.SetResourceVersion(passedRV)
410: 		} else { // copy status from original object
411: 			if err := copyStatusFrom(oldObject, obj); err != nil {
412: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to copy the status for object with status subresource: %w", err)
413: 			}
414: 		}
415: 	} else if isStatus {
416: 		return apierrors.NewNotFound(gvr.GroupResource(), accessor.GetName())
417: 	}
418: 
419: 	oldAccessor, err := meta.Accessor(oldObject)
420: 	if err != nil {
421: 		return err
422: 	}
423: 
424: 	// If the new object does not have the resource version set and it allows unconditional update,
425: 	// default it to the resource version of the existing resource
426: 	if accessor.GetResourceVersion() == "" && allowsUnconditionalUpdate(gvk) {
427: 		accessor.SetResourceVersion(oldAccessor.GetResourceVersion())
428: 	}
429: 	if accessor.GetResourceVersion() != oldAccessor.GetResourceVersion() {
430: 		return apierrors.NewConflict(gvr.GroupResource(), accessor.GetName(), errors.New("object was modified"))
431: 	}
432: 	if oldAccessor.GetResourceVersion() == "" {
433: 		oldAccessor.SetResourceVersion("0")
434: 	}
435: 	intResourceVersion, err := strconv.ParseUint(oldAccessor.GetResourceVersion(), 10, 64)
436: 	if err != nil {
437: 		return fmt.Errorf("can not convert resourceVersion %q to int: %w", oldAccessor.GetResourceVersion(), err)
438: 	}
439: 	intResourceVersion++
440: 	accessor.SetResourceVersion(strconv.FormatUint(intResourceVersion, 10))
441: 
442: 	if !deleting && !deletionTimestampEqual(accessor, oldAccessor) {
443: 		return fmt.Errorf("error: Unable to edit %s: metadata.deletionTimestamp field is immutable", accessor.GetName())
444: 	}
445: 
446: 	if !accessor.GetDeletionTimestamp().IsZero() && len(accessor.GetFinalizers()) == 0 {
447: 		return t.ObjectTracker.Delete(gvr, accessor.GetNamespace(), accessor.GetName())
448: 	}
449: 	obj, err = convertFromUnstructuredIfNecessary(t.scheme, obj)
450: 	if err != nil {
451: 		return err
452: 	}
453: 	return t.ObjectTracker.Update(gvr, obj, ns)
454: }

589: func (c *fakeClient) filterWithFields(list []runtime.Object, gvk schema.GroupVersionKind, fs fields.Selector) ([]runtime.Object, error) {
590: 	requiresExact := selector.RequiresExactMatch(fs)
591: 	if !requiresExact {
592: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("field selector %s is not in one of the two supported forms \"key==val\" or \"key=val\"",
593: 			fs)
594: 	}
595: 
596: 	// Field selection is mimicked via indexes, so there's no sane answer this function can give
597: 	// if there are no indexes registered for the GroupVersionKind of the objects in the list.
598: 	indexes := c.indexes[gvk]
599: 	for _, req := range fs.Requirements() {
600: 		if len(indexes) == 0 || indexes[req.Field] == nil {
601: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("List on GroupVersionKind %v specifies selector on field %s, but no "+
602: 				"index with name %s has been registered for GroupVersionKind %v", gvk, req.Field, req.Field, gvk)
603: 		}
604: 	}
605: 
606: 	filteredList := make([]runtime.Object, 0, len(list))
607: 	for _, obj := range list {
608: 		matches := true
609: 		for _, req := range fs.Requirements() {
610: 			indexExtractor := indexes[req.Field]
611: 			if !c.objMatchesFieldSelector(obj, indexExtractor, req.Value) {
612: 				matches = false
613: 				break
614: 			}
615: 		}
616: 		if matches {
617: 			filteredList = append(filteredList, obj)
618: 		}
619: 	}
620: 	return filteredList, nil
621: }

630: 		if extractedVal == val {
631: 			return true

804: func (c *fakeClient) patch(obj client.Object, patch client.Patch, opts ...client.PatchOption) error {

806: 	patchOptions.ApplyOptions(opts)
807: 
808: 	for _, dryRunOpt := range patchOptions.DryRun {
809: 		if dryRunOpt == metav1.DryRunAll {
810: 			return nil
811: 		}
812: 	}
813: 
814: 	gvr, err := getGVRFromObject(obj, c.scheme)
815: 	if err != nil {
816: 		return err
817: 	}
818: 	accessor, err := meta.Accessor(obj)
819: 	if err != nil {
820: 		return err
821: 	}
822: 	data, err := patch.Data(obj)
823: 	if err != nil {
824: 		return err
825: 	}
826: 
827: 	gvk, err := apiutil.GVKForObject(obj, c.scheme)
828: 	if err != nil {
829: 		return err
830: 	}
831: 
832: 	oldObj, err := c.tracker.Get(gvr, accessor.GetNamespace(), accessor.GetName())
833: 	if err != nil {
834: 		return err
835: 	}
836: 	oldAccessor, err := meta.Accessor(oldObj)

838: 		return err
839: 	}

841: 	// Apply patch without updating object.
842: 	// To remain in accordance with the behavior of k8s api behavior,
843: 	// a patch must not allow for changes to the deletionTimestamp of an object.
844: 	// The reaction() function applies the patch to the object and calls Update(),
845: 	// whereas dryPatch() replicates this behavior but skips the call to Update().
846: 	// This ensures that the patch may be rejected if a deletionTimestamp is modified, prior
847: 	// to updating the object.
848: 	action := testing.NewPatchAction(gvr, accessor.GetNamespace(), accessor.GetName(), patch.Type(), data)
849: 	o, err := dryPatch(action, c.tracker)
850: 	if err != nil {
851: 		return err
852: 	}
853: 	newObj, err := meta.Accessor(o)
854: 	if err != nil {
855: 		return err
856: 	}

858: 	// Validate that deletionTimestamp has not been changed
859: 	if !deletionTimestampEqual(newObj, oldAccessor) {
860: 		return fmt.Errorf("rejected patch, metadata.deletionTimestamp immutable")
861: 	}
862: 
863: 	reaction := testing.ObjectReaction(c.tracker)
864: 	handled, o, err := reaction(action)
865: 	if err != nil {
866: 		return err
867: 	}
868: 	if !handled {
869: 		panic("tracker could not handle patch method")
870: 	}
871: 
872: 	if _, isUnstructured := obj.(runtime.Unstructured); isUnstructured {
873: 		ta, err := meta.TypeAccessor(o)
874: 		if err != nil {
875: 			return err
876: 		}
877: 		ta.SetKind(gvk.Kind)
878: 		ta.SetAPIVersion(gvk.GroupVersion().String())
879: 	}
880: 
881: 	j, err := json.Marshal(o)
882: 	if err != nil {
883: 		return err
884: 	}
885: 	zero(obj)
886: 	return json.Unmarshal(j, obj)
887: }

889: // Applying a patch results in a deletionTimestamp that is truncated to the nearest second.
890: // Check that the diff between a new and old deletion timestamp is within a reasonable threshold
891: // to be considered unchanged.
892: func deletionTimestampEqual(newObj metav1.Object, obj metav1.Object) bool {
893: 	newTime := newObj.GetDeletionTimestamp()
894: 	oldTime := obj.GetDeletionTimestamp()
895: 
896: 	if newTime == nil || oldTime == nil {
897: 		return newTime == oldTime
898: 	}
899: 	return newTime.Time.Sub(oldTime.Time).Abs() < time.Second
900: }

902: // The behavior of applying the patch is pulled out into dryPatch(),
903: // which applies the patch and returns an object, but does not Update() the object.
904: // This function returns a patched runtime object that may then be validated before a call to Update() is executed.
905: // This results in some code duplication, but was found to be a cleaner alternative than unmarshalling and introspecting the patch data
906: // and easier than refactoring the k8s client-go method upstream.
907: // Duplicate of upstream: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/783d0d33626e59d55d52bfd7696b775851f92107/testing/fixture.go#L146-L194
908: func dryPatch(action testing.PatchActionImpl, tracker testing.ObjectTracker) (runtime.Object, error) {
909: 	ns := action.GetNamespace()
910: 	gvr := action.GetResource()
911: 
912: 	obj, err := tracker.Get(gvr, ns, action.GetName())
913: 	if err != nil {
914: 		return nil, err
915: 	}
916: 
917: 	old, err := json.Marshal(obj)
918: 	if err != nil {
919: 		return nil, err
920: 	}
921: 
922: 	// reset the object in preparation to unmarshal, since unmarshal does not guarantee that fields
923: 	// in obj that are removed by patch are cleared
924: 	value := reflect.ValueOf(obj)
925: 	value.Elem().Set(reflect.New(value.Type().Elem()).Elem())
926: 
927: 	switch action.GetPatchType() {
928: 	case types.JSONPatchType:
929: 		patch, err := jsonpatch.DecodePatch(action.GetPatch())
930: 		if err != nil {
931: 			return nil, err
932: 		}
933: 		modified, err := patch.Apply(old)
934: 		if err != nil {
935: 			return nil, err
936: 		}
937: 
938: 		if err = json.Unmarshal(modified, obj); err != nil {
939: 			return nil, err
940: 		}
941: 	case types.MergePatchType:
942: 		modified, err := jsonpatch.MergePatch(old, action.GetPatch())
943: 		if err != nil {
944: 			return nil, err
945: 		}

This is incomplete and misleading. In reality, the read behavior depends on configuration: when `Options.Cache` and `Options.Cache.Reader` are both set, reads may be served from a local cache instead of hitting the API server, with specific exceptions (e.g., `Options.Cache.DisableFor` and `Options.Cache.Unstructured`). Write operations, however, always go directly to the API server. The comments need to be updated to accurately describe this behavior.

    The goal is to clarify the read/write semantics of the client in the public API documentation, making it clear that reads may come from a cache (when configured) while writes always target the API server. This is purely a documentation change — no functional behavior should be altered.

153: // addKnownGroupAndReload reloads the mapper with updated information about missing API group.
154: // versions can be specified for partial updates, for instance for v1beta1 version only.
155: func (m *mapper) addKnownGroupAndReload(groupName string, versions ...string) error {
156: 	// versions will here be [""] if the forwarded Version value of
157: 	// GroupVersionResource (in calling method) was not specified.
158: 	if len(versions) == 1 && versions[0] == "" {
159: 		versions = nil
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	// If no specific versions are set by user, we will scan all available ones for the API group.
163: 	// This operation requires 2 requests: /api and /apis, but only once. For all subsequent calls
164: 	// this data will be taken from cache.
165: 	if len(versions) == 0 {
166: 		apiGroup, err := m.findAPIGroupByName(groupName)
167: 		if err != nil {
168: 			return err
169: 		}
170: 		if apiGroup != nil {
171: 			for _, version := range apiGroup.Versions {
172: 				versions = append(versions, version.Version)
173: 			}
174: 		}
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	m.mu.Lock()
178: 	defer m.mu.Unlock()
179: 
180: 	// Create or fetch group resources from cache.
181: 	groupResources := &restmapper.APIGroupResources{
182: 		Group:              metav1.APIGroup{Name: groupName},
183: 		VersionedResources: make(map[string][]metav1.APIResource),
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	// Update information for group resources about versioned resources.
187: 	// The number of API calls is equal to the number of versions: /apis/<group>/<version>.
188: 	// If we encounter a missing API version (NotFound error), we will remove the group from
189: 	// the m.apiGroups and m.knownGroups caches.
190: 	// If this happens, in the next call the group will be added back to apiGroups
191: 	// and only the existing versions will be loaded in knownGroups.
192: 	groupVersionResources, err := m.fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked(groupName, versions...)
193: 	if err != nil {
194: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get API group resources: %w", err)
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	if _, ok := m.knownGroups[groupName]; ok {
198: 		groupResources = m.knownGroups[groupName]
199: 	}
200: 
201: 	// Update information for group resources about the API group by adding new versions.
202: 	// Ignore the versions that are already registered.
203: 	for groupVersion, resources := range groupVersionResources {
204: 		version := groupVersion.Version
205: 
206: 		groupResources.VersionedResources[version] = resources.APIResources
207: 		found := false
208: 		for _, v := range groupResources.Group.Versions {
209: 			if v.Version == version {
210: 				found = true
211: 				break
212: 			}
213: 		}
214: 
215: 		if !found {
216: 			groupResources.Group.Versions = append(groupResources.Group.Versions, metav1.GroupVersionForDiscovery{
217: 				GroupVersion: metav1.GroupVersion{Group: groupName, Version: version}.String(),
218: 				Version:      version,
219: 			})
220: 		}
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	// Update data in the cache.
224: 	m.knownGroups[groupName] = groupResources
225: 
226: 	// Finally, update the group with received information and regenerate the mapper.
227: 	updatedGroupResources := make([]*restmapper.APIGroupResources, 0, len(m.knownGroups))
228: 	for _, agr := range m.knownGroups {
229: 		updatedGroupResources = append(updatedGroupResources, agr)
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	m.mapper = restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper(updatedGroupResources)
233: 	return nil
234: }

237: func (m *mapper) findAPIGroupByName(groupName string) (*metav1.APIGroup, error) {
238: 	// Looking in the cache first.
239: 	{
240: 		m.mu.RLock()
241: 		group, ok := m.apiGroups[groupName]
242: 		m.mu.RUnlock()
243: 		if ok {
244: 			return group, nil
245: 		}
246: 	}

248: 	// Update the cache if nothing was found.
249: 	apiGroups, err := m.client.ServerGroups()
250: 	if err != nil {
251: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get server groups: %w", err)
252: 	}
253: 	if len(apiGroups.Groups) == 0 {
254: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("received an empty API groups list")

258: 	for i := range apiGroups.Groups {

261: 	}
262: 	m.mu.Unlock()

276: 	groupVersionResources := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]*metav1.APIResourceList)
277: 	failedGroups := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]error)

We need to address a flakiness issue in envtest where tests that expect the `default` namespace to be immediately available after control plane startup can fail. When etcd is brought up for the first time, there can be a delay before the `default` namespace is actually created and visible to the apiserver.

    The goal is to add a polling mechanism that waits for the `default` namespace to become available in the apiserver immediately after the control plane starts, before proceeding with the rest of the startup process (CRD installation, webhook installation, etc.).

    Specifically, in `pkg/envtest/server.go`, after the control plane has started and a REST config has been created, we should poll the apiserver for the existence of the `default` namespace. The wait should be bounded (e.g., a 5-second timeout) and should poll at a reasonably fast interval (e.g., every 50 milliseconds) to avoid unnecessary delays. If the namespace doesn't become available within the timeout, startup should fail with a clear error message.

    Please ensure this wait only happens when starting up a new control plane (not when using an existing cluster), and that it occurs before any CRD or webhook installation steps.

## Environment Setup
Check the `Makefile` and `go.mod` at the repository root for build and test targets. There are also helper scripts in the `hack/` directory (e.g., `hack/test-all.sh`, `hack/verify.sh`, `hack/check-everything.sh`) that may be useful for understanding how to run tests.

## Implementation Plan
- Add a new private method `waitForDefaultNamespace` on the `Environment` struct that accepts a `*rest.Config` and creates a controller-runtime client.
    - Within this method, use a polling utility (e.g., `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout`) to repeatedly attempt to get the `default` namespace via the client, ignoring "not found" errors and returning `false, nil` to continue polling.
    - Configure the poll with a short interval (about 50ms) and a total timeout (about 5 seconds).
    - In the `Start()` method, call this new method after the control plane has started and the admin user config has been established, but only when not using an existing cluster.

## Problem

  The lazy REST mapper in `pkg/client/apiutil/restmapper.go` maintains two separate caches:
  - `apiGroups`: caches the list of API groups and their versions (populated from `ServerGroups()`)
  - `knownGroups`: caches the group resources and their versioned resources (populated from `ServerResourcesForGroupVersion()`)

  When a group version is not found by `ServerResourcesForGroupVersion()`, the current implementation only invalidates the caches if `isGroupVersionCached()` returns true. This check only looks at the `knownGroups` cache.

  However, there's a race condition window: if a version is removed from the API server, it's possible that the group version is cached in `apiGroups` but NOT yet cached in `knownGroups`. In that scenario:

  - An error is returned instead of the version being silently skipped

  - Each cache should be checked and invalidated independently:
    - If the group version is in `apiGroups`, remove it from there
    - If the group version is in `knownGroups`, remove it from there

153: // addKnownGroupAndReload reloads the mapper with updated information about missing API group.
154: // versions can be specified for partial updates, for instance for v1beta1 version only.
155: func (m *mapper) addKnownGroupAndReload(groupName string, versions ...string) error {
156: 	// versions will here be [""] if the forwarded Version value of
157: 	// GroupVersionResource (in calling method) was not specified.
158: 	if len(versions) == 1 && versions[0] == "" {
159: 		versions = nil
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	// If no specific versions are set by user, we will scan all available ones for the API group.
163: 	// This operation requires 2 requests: /api and /apis, but only once. For all subsequent calls
164: 	// this data will be taken from cache.
165: 	if len(versions) == 0 {
166: 		apiGroup, err := m.findAPIGroupByName(groupName)
167: 		if err != nil {
168: 			return err
169: 		}
170: 		if apiGroup != nil {
171: 			for _, version := range apiGroup.Versions {
172: 				versions = append(versions, version.Version)
173: 			}
174: 		}
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	m.mu.Lock()
178: 	defer m.mu.Unlock()
179: 
180: 	// Create or fetch group resources from cache.
181: 	groupResources := &restmapper.APIGroupResources{
182: 		Group:              metav1.APIGroup{Name: groupName},
183: 		VersionedResources: make(map[string][]metav1.APIResource),
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	// Update information for group resources about versioned resources.
187: 	// The number of API calls is equal to the number of versions: /apis/<group>/<version>.
188: 	// If we encounter a missing API version (NotFound error), we will remove the group from
189: 	// the m.apiGroups and m.knownGroups caches.
190: 	// If this happens, in the next call the group will be added back to apiGroups
191: 	// and only the existing versions will be loaded in knownGroups.
192: 	groupVersionResources, err := m.fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked(groupName, versions...)
193: 	if err != nil {
194: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get API group resources: %w", err)
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	if _, ok := m.knownGroups[groupName]; ok {
198: 		groupResources = m.knownGroups[groupName]
199: 	}
200: 
201: 	// Update information for group resources about the API group by adding new versions.
202: 	// Ignore the versions that are already registered.
203: 	for groupVersion, resources := range groupVersionResources {
204: 		version := groupVersion.Version
205: 
206: 		groupResources.VersionedResources[version] = resources.APIResources
207: 		found := false
208: 		for _, v := range groupResources.Group.Versions {
209: 			if v.Version == version {
210: 				found = true
211: 				break
212: 			}
213: 		}
214: 
215: 		if !found {
216: 			groupResources.Group.Versions = append(groupResources.Group.Versions, metav1.GroupVersionForDiscovery{
217: 				GroupVersion: metav1.GroupVersion{Group: groupName, Version: version}.String(),
218: 				Version:      version,
219: 			})
220: 		}
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	// Update data in the cache.
224: 	m.knownGroups[groupName] = groupResources
225: 
226: 	// Finally, update the group with received information and regenerate the mapper.
227: 	updatedGroupResources := make([]*restmapper.APIGroupResources, 0, len(m.knownGroups))
228: 	for _, agr := range m.knownGroups {
229: 		updatedGroupResources = append(updatedGroupResources, agr)
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	m.mapper = restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper(updatedGroupResources)
233: 	return nil
234: }

236: // findAPIGroupByNameLocked returns API group by its name.
237: func (m *mapper) findAPIGroupByName(groupName string) (*metav1.APIGroup, error) {
238: 	// Looking in the cache first.
239: 	{
240: 		m.mu.RLock()
241: 		group, ok := m.apiGroups[groupName]
242: 		m.mu.RUnlock()
243: 		if ok {
244: 			return group, nil
245: 		}
246: 	}
247: 
248: 	// Update the cache if nothing was found.
249: 	apiGroups, err := m.client.ServerGroups()
250: 	if err != nil {
251: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get server groups: %w", err)
252: 	}
253: 	if len(apiGroups.Groups) == 0 {
254: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("received an empty API groups list")
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	m.mu.Lock()
258: 	for i := range apiGroups.Groups {
259: 		group := &apiGroups.Groups[i]
260: 		m.apiGroups[group.Name] = group
261: 	}
262: 	m.mu.Unlock()
263: 
264: 	// Looking in the cache again.
265: 	m.mu.RLock()
266: 	defer m.mu.RUnlock()
267: 
268: 	// Don't return an error here if the API group is not present.
269: 	// The reloaded RESTMapper will take care of returning a NoMatchError.
270: 	return m.apiGroups[groupName], nil
271: }

273: // fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked fetches the resources for the specified group and its versions.
274: // This method might modify the cache so it needs to be called under the lock.
275: func (m *mapper) fetchGroupVersionResourcesLocked(groupName string, versions ...string) (map[schema.GroupVersion]*metav1.APIResourceList, error) {
276: 	groupVersionResources := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]*metav1.APIResourceList)
277: 	failedGroups := make(map[schema.GroupVersion]error)
278: 
279: 	for _, version := range versions {
280: 		groupVersion := schema.GroupVersion{Group: groupName, Version: version}
281: 
282: 		apiResourceList, err := m.client.ServerResourcesForGroupVersion(groupVersion.String())
283: 		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) {
284: 			// If the version is not found, we remove the group from the cache
285: 			// so it gets refreshed on the next call.
286: 			if m.isAPIGroupCached(groupVersion) {
287: 				delete(m.apiGroups, groupName)
288: 			}
289: 			if m.isGroupVersionCached(groupVersion) {
290: 				delete(m.knownGroups, groupName)
291: 			}
292: 			continue
293: 		} else if err != nil {
294: 			failedGroups[groupVersion] = err
295: 		}
296: 
297: 		if apiResourceList != nil {
298: 			// even in case of error, some fallback might have been returned.
299: 			groupVersionResources[groupVersion] = apiResourceList
300: 		}
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	if len(failedGroups) > 0 {
304: 		err := ErrResourceDiscoveryFailed(failedGroups)
305: 		return nil, &err
306: 	}
307: 
308: 	return groupVersionResources, nil
309: }
310: 
311: // isGroupVersionCached checks if a version for a group is cached in the known groups cache.
312: func (m *mapper) isGroupVersionCached(gv schema.GroupVersion) bool {
313: 	if cachedGroup, ok := m.knownGroups[gv.Group]; ok {
314: 		_, cached := cachedGroup.VersionedResources[gv.Version]
315: 		return cached
316: 	}
317: 
318: 	return false
319: }
320: 
321: // isAPIGroupCached checks if a version for a group is cached in the api groups cache.
322: func (m *mapper) isAPIGroupCached(gv schema.GroupVersion) bool {
323: 	cachedGroup, ok := m.apiGroups[gv.Group]
324: 	if !ok {
325: 		return false
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	for _, version := range cachedGroup.Versions {
329: 		if version.Version == gv.Version {
330: 			return true
331: 		}
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	return false
335: }
